notes: The binding is not generated on this platform and that is structural rather than a configuration choice: the SDK ships clang 15 on both the 5.1 and 6.1 lines, while V8 145's vendored libc++ announces it supports clang 20 and later and uses __builtin_clzg/__builtin_ctzg, added in clang 19. bindgen therefore fails after the whole C++ side has already built. scripts/build-v8-ohos.sh feeds the committed src_binding.rs through V8_PREBUILT_BINDING and refuses if it is missing. The binding encodes V8's FFI ABI for a rusty_v8 revision rather than a target's calling convention, so it is byte-identical to the Android one at this revision and both OpenHarmony triples are LP64.

required_patches.notes: Upstream Chromium has no OpenHarmony support at all: target_os is in no whitelist and neither build/ nor buildtools/ mentions it. This patch creates build/toolchain/ohos/BUILD.gn, which is the only thing that makes a custom_toolchain for the platform expressible. It creates a file rather than modifying one, which is why the Android proof can account for it with --accounted-patch.

sdk.notes: The OpenHarmony native SDK supplies the target sysroot and the musl libc this archive links against, so it is part of the artifact's identity the same way the NDK is on Android. Pinned to the SDK that produced the verified archive rather than to the newest available. ohos_api is what V8 was compiled against, which is this SDK's own API level; the product floor a consumer sees is declared separately by scripts/build-ohos-sdk.sh and is allowed to be higher.
